questions.q: Define verbal irony and give one example from "cktkj n'kZu" where a character says something but means the opposite.
questions.a: Verbal irony occurs when a speaker's intended meaning is the opposite of the literal words spoken. In the story, when Hkxr th says "My nose is the pride of my lineage" while everyone sees it as ordinary, he is using verbal irony — his words inflate his nose's importance, but the reality undercuts him. A wrong answer would confuse verbal irony with sarcasm (which is harsher and directed at someone) or miss that the irony here is unconscious, revealing the character's delusion.

questions.q: Explain the difference between situational irony and dramatic irony. Which one operates when Hkxr th loses his nose at the fair while trying to protect it?
questions.a: Situational irony arises when the outcome of a situation is the opposite of what was expected; dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows something the character does not. Hkxr th's loss of his nose while guarding it is situational irony — his protective actions directly cause the loss. A wrong answer would label it dramatic irony (the audience doesn't have superior knowledge here) or call it mere bad luck, missing the structural reversal that defines situational irony.

questions.q: Identify a symbol in the story other than the nose. Describe what it represents and quote a brief textual detail (paraphrased) that supports your interpretation.
questions.a: The fair (mela) symbolizes the chaotic, superficial world where false values are traded. When Hkxr th enters the fair seeking validation, the noise, crowds, and trivial disputes mirror the hollow social arena where his pride is exposed. A weak answer would pick the nose again or choose an object like the "stick" without linking it to a broader idea, showing an inability to extend symbolic reading beyond the central image.

questions.q: Compare the function of irony and symbolism in the story's climax. How do they work together to deliver the author's critique of false pride?
questions.a: At the climax, situational irony (the nose is lost while being protected) and symbolism (the nose as hollow pride) converge: the physical loss enacts the symbolic truth that his pride was always fragile. The irony makes the symbol visceral — the reader feels the collapse, not just understands it. A poor answer would treat them as separate devices, missing their synergy in reinforcing the theme.

questions.q: Evaluate this statement: "The story uses irony only for humor; its symbolism is heavy-handed." Defend or refute with two specific textual reasons.
questions.a: Refute. First, the irony is tragicomic — Hkxr th's downfall evokes pity, not just laughter, because his delusion is human. Second, the symbolism is layered: the nose represents not just pride but also identity, social performance, and the body as a site of honor. A wrong answer would agree, revealing a surface reading that misses the story's satirical depth and the nuance of its central symbol.

questions.q: Write a 4-line paragraph continuing the story after Hkxr th loses his nose, using one ironic statement and one new symbol to show his changed perspective.
questions.a: A strong response might have Hkxr th say, "Now I truly have the perfect nose — N/A at all," (verbal irony) and introduce a mirror as a new symbol of self-confrontation. A weak response would lack irony or use a symbol without clear representational meaning, showing the student cannot generate original literary applications.
